# Evidence for adopting Acme parser for large nested documents

## Scope

This report assesses whether the three supplied local records support adopting Acme parser release 2 for large nested documents. It covers measured parse time and memory, the relevance of the tested documents, and evidence still needed for an adoption decision.

## Findings

### Performance on nested documents

North Lab tested Acme releases 1 and 2 on 100 nested 20 MB documents, running each version once per document. It reports that release 2 used 15% less parse time and 40% more peak memory [1]. This is the only supplied test of nested documents, and North Lab is independent of the vendor [1][2][3]. **Inference:** the result supports a possible parse-time benefit for documents resembling that sample, alongside a material memory cost; it does not establish that adopting release 2 improves overall production performance [1].

### What the vendor benchmark establishes

The Acme team reports a 30% parse-time reduction for release 2 against release 1 across 500 runs on one laptop, using flat 1 KB documents. It did not measure memory and excluded nested documents [2]. The later Acme announcement repeats that result without a new experiment [3]. These records establish what the vendor reported about its flat-document test, but provide no direct measurement for large nested documents [2][3].

### Weight of the evidence

The vendor release is a first-hand account of its own benchmark, but its flat 1 KB input is poorly matched to the target workload [2]. **Source-appraisal inference:** as the developer of release 2, Acme has an incentive to present favourable performance results [2]. The blog is a derivative retelling, so it adds no independent corroboration [3]. The more recent North Lab record directly tests nested 20 MB documents and provides an independent measurement, making it more applicable to this question [1]. Its single run per version on each document and limited reported methods leave the stability and generality of the measured differences uncertain [1]. **Inference:** the supplied evidence is too narrow to justify an unconditional adoption decision for production use [1][2][3].

## Conflicts

The vendor reports 30% less parse time on flat 1 KB documents, while North Lab reports 15% less parse time on nested 20 MB documents [1][2]. These figures differ, but the input types and test procedures differ too; they are not conflicting measurements of the same workload. The vendor's later blog repeats its release figure and is not a separate result [2][3].

## Limitations

North Lab ran each release only once per document and gives no variability, hardware, parser configuration, document characteristics beyond size and nesting, or production workload mix in the supplied record [1]. The reliability of the 15% time and 40% memory differences across systems and documents is therefore unresolved. This is missing evidence, not evidence that the differences would disappear.

The lab did not evaluate malformed data or production throughput, and the vendor records report no tests of those behaviours for large nested documents [1][2][3]. The supplied records therefore do not establish error handling, sustained throughput, or whether the measured peak-memory increase fits the intended deployment's limits [1][2][3].

The comparison is between Acme releases 1 and 2, not against the parser currently used by the prospective adopter [1][2]. The records do not supply that baseline or an adoption threshold, so the practical value of switching remains unknown.

This appraisal is limited to the three supplied local records. No underlying data, code, or fuller study methods were provided in those records [1][2][3].

## Sources

1. [Independent parser study](../sources/lab-study.md) — North Lab, published 2026-09-25.
2. [Acme release 2](../sources/vendor-release.md) — Acme parser team, published 2026-09-20.
3. [Acme performance announcement](../sources/vendor-blog.md) — Acme parser team, published 2026-09-21.

Architecture review · 1 material direction

One owner for the delivery fee rule

An Order must receive the same delivery fee quote at checkout and renewal. The two flows currently calculate that fee independently, although their rules agree today.

  • PRODUCT.md requires equal delivery fee quotes at checkout and renewal; GLOSSARY.md defines “delivery fee” and “Order”.

docs/features/sender-receipt-status/spec.content:
# Sender receipt status view

> **Authority:** This specification records the confirmed feature intent and selected solution. It is ready for ticket decomposition when the readiness statement below is satisfied.

## Feature overview

A sender can open a receipt status link and see the latest authorised status of a parcel previously accepted by the relay, together with the time that status was updated. This refines [CAP-03 and SEC-01](../../../PRODUCT.md). A [receipt](../../../GLOSSARY.md) acknowledges acceptance by the relay; it does not prove delivery to the recipient. The approved direction is recorded in [the confirmed feature brief](../../../confirmed-feature.md).

The [current contract](../../../src/status-contract.txt) can find a receipt and the existing authentication supplies a validated sender identity. There is currently no browser status page.

## Problem, outcomes, and success measures

The sender has no browser view for checking an accepted parcel's current status. The outcome is an accessible, read-only view of the latest status and its update time for a receipt the sender owns, while keeping receipt ownership private. The confirmed brief sets no numeric success measure or timed freshness guarantee.

## Scope and non-goals

### In scope

- Open a receipt status link using the existing session, including a sign-in return when that session has expired.
- Show the authorised receipt's status and update time, or an appropriate unavailable, loading, or recoverable error state.
- Let keyboard and screen-reader users obtain the complete outcome and retry a failed read.

### Non-goals

- Editing status, exporting records, live tracking, or admin access.
- Recipient delivery proof or a timed freshness guarantee.

## Actors, goals, and use cases

### ACT-01: Sender

The sender wants to check the current state of a parcel that the relay accepted without gaining access to another sender's parcel.

### UC-01: Check a receipt

- **Actor:** Sender.
- **Trigger:** Opens a receipt status link.
- **Preconditions:** The link identifies a receipt; a valid session identifies the sender for an authorised read.
- **Successful outcome:** The page shows the owned receipt's latest status and update time.
- **Alternatives and exceptions:** An unknown or another sender's receipt produces the same unavailable outcome. An expired session sends the sender to sign-in and preserves the receipt destination for return. Loading is announced. A failed read offers retry; if a previous read succeeded, its result remains visible with stale/error feedback until a new read succeeds.

## Feature intent

### Requirements and rules

- **REQ-01: Authorised status:** For a valid owned receipt, show its latest status and update time. The allowed status values are **Accepted**, **In transit**, **Delivered**, and **Failed**.
- **REQ-02: Ownership privacy:** An unknown receipt and a receipt owned by another sender produce the same unavailable message, without disclosing which condition occurred.
- **REQ-03: Session return:** If the session has expired, require sign-in and preserve the requested receipt destination for return after authentication.
- **REQ-04: Read recovery:** Announce loading and allow retry after a request error. A failed read must not replace the last successfully read status; keep that result visible with stale/error feedback. A retry shows a new status only after a new read succeeds.
- **REQ-05: Accessible outcome:** The complete status, update time, unavailable outcome, sign-in path, loading feedback, and error/retry interaction must be accessible by keyboard and screen reader.
- **REQ-06: Receipt meaning:** Present the status as a relay status for an accepted parcel, without implying recipient proof.

### Experience and design requirements

The status and update time form one understandable result. The unavailable message is identical for missing and unauthorised receipts. Loading and error feedback are exposed to assistive technology; retry is operable without a pointer. When a previous successful result is retained after an error, the page makes clear that it is stale rather than presenting it as a newly confirmed status.

### Quality and external constraints

Status access is restricted to the sender identified by the validated session. There is no selected maximum age for a displayed result and no timed freshness promise. This feature is read-only.

### Scenarios and acceptance

#### SC-01: Owned receipt

- **Given:** A sender has a valid session and owns the receipt in the link.
- **When:** The sender opens the link and the read succeeds.
- **Then:** The page shows that receipt's latest allowed status and its update time.

**Covers:** REQ-01, REQ-06.

#### SC-02: Receipt unavailable

- **Given:** A sender has a valid session.
- **When:** The sender opens a link to an unknown receipt or one owned by another sender.
- **Then:** The page gives the same unavailable message in either case and exposes no receipt details.

**Covers:** REQ-02.

#### SC-03: Session expired

- **Given:** The sender's session has expired.
- **When:** The sender opens a receipt status link.
- **Then:** Sign-in is required, and the sender can return to the requested receipt destination after authentication.

**Covers:** REQ-03.

#### SC-04: Failed read and retry

- **Given:** The page has a previously successful status result.
- **When:** A subsequent read fails and the sender retries.
- **Then:** Loading and error feedback are accessible, the previous result remains visible and identified as stale, and no new status appears unless the retry read succeeds.

**Covers:** REQ-04, REQ-05.

#### SC-05: Initial read fails

- **Given:** The page has no successful status result.
- **When:** Its read fails.
- **Then:** An accessible error and retry action are available; no status is presented as successfully read.

**Covers:** REQ-04, REQ-05.

#### Acceptance conditions

- **ACC-01:** Every permitted status outcome includes the update time and can be understood and operated by keyboard and screen-reader users.
- **ACC-02:** The status view does not reveal whether an unavailable receipt exists or belongs to someone else.
- **ACC-03:** Authentication interruption and request failure each have the confirmed recovery path, without replacing a successful result on a failed read.

## Selected solution

### Design drivers and current context

The [current status contract](../../../src/status-contract.txt) defines `findReceipt(receiptId)` as returning `{receiptId, senderId, currentStatus, updatedAt}` or not-found. Existing authentication exposes `senderId` from a validated session. The browser page does not yet exist. Ownership privacy (REQ-02), session return (REQ-03), and retained results on failure (REQ-04) shape the selected boundary and page behaviour.

### Strategy and material decisions

Add a browser receipt status page backed by the existing validated session and `findReceipt` contract. The status read checks ownership before returning any details. Missing and forbidden receipts map to one unavailable response. The page does not write receipt data. The existing data source and session contract remain in use; no migration or new dependency is needed.

### Responsibilities and boundaries

- The browser page requests and displays status, update time, loading, unavailable, and error/retry states. It retains the last successful result across a failed later read.
- The authenticated read boundary obtains the session sender, looks up the receipt, checks ownership, and returns details only for an owned receipt.
- Authentication handles an expired session and returns the sender to the preserved receipt destination after sign-in.

### Interfaces and data contracts

The read takes a receipt identifier from the requested destination and uses the validated session sender identity. For an owned receipt, its read-only status response exposes only `receiptId`, `currentStatus`, and `updatedAt`. `currentStatus` is one of the four values in REQ-01; `updatedAt` is the status update time from the existing receipt contract. `senderId` is used for authorisation and is not part of the status response. Missing and forbidden records have one indistinguishable unavailable response. A request failure is distinct from that unavailable outcome and permits retry.

### Data and lifecycle

The existing receipt is the status source. Each successful read replaces the displayed result with the status and update time it returned. A failed read does not replace the last successful result; the retained result receives stale/error feedback until a successful read replaces it. No new stored data, status transition, migration, or write path is selected.

### Integrations and failure handling

The page uses existing authentication and receipt lookup. An expired session leads to sign-in with the original destination preserved. A lookup that is missing or fails ownership checks yields the shared unavailable outcome. A request error yields an error state with retry, which issues another read. Only a successful read may update the displayed status.

### Cross-cutting and operational design

The ownership check precedes disclosure of receipt fields. The browser interaction includes keyboard and screen-reader access to loading, status, time, unavailability, sign-in, and retry. No live updates or time-based refresh promise is selected.

### Verification seams

- **Authenticated status lookup:** Establish that an owned receipt returns only the selected fields, while missing and other-sender receipts produce the same unavailable response.
- **Browser interaction:** Establish the owned result, loading announcement, expired-session return, keyboard and screen-reader outcomes, and error/retry behaviour with and without a prior successful result.

## Dependencies, assumptions, risks, and unresolved items

- **DEP-01: Existing contracts:** The solution uses the documented `findReceipt` result and validated session sender identity in [current-system evidence](../../../src/status-contract.txt). These support REQ-01 to REQ-03 and the selected read boundary.
- **RSK-01: Ownership disclosure:** Distinct missing and forbidden responses could reveal receipt ownership. The shared unavailable response and ownership check before returning details address REQ-02.
- **Unresolved items:** None. The confirmed brief selects no timed freshness guarantee, so no freshness threshold is needed for decomposition.

## Traceability and readiness

| Confirmed intent | Selected solution | Verification seam |
| --- | --- | --- |
| REQ-01, REQ-06 | Read-only page and authorised response with status and update time | Authenticated lookup; browser result |
| REQ-02 | Ownership check and shared unavailable response | Authenticated lookup; unavailable view |
| REQ-03 | Existing session and preserved sign-in destination | Browser sign-in return |
| REQ-04, REQ-05 | Retained successful result, accessible feedback, and retry read | Browser interaction |

### Readiness statement

The [confirmed brief](../../../confirmed-feature.md) settles the observable behaviour and selected solution, and the [current-system contract](../../../src/status-contract.txt) supports the integration boundary. Ticket decomposition can proceed without choosing a material solution or inventing feature behaviour.

# Feature specification: Sender receipt status

## Purpose and scope

Refine CAP-03 and SEC-01 so an authenticated sender can open a receipt status link and see the latest authorised status of a parcel that the relay previously accepted, together with the time that status was updated. A receipt acknowledges acceptance by the relay; it is not proof of delivery to a recipient.

This feature covers a read-only browser status page and an authenticated status lookup for the session sender. It does not cover status editing, record export, live tracking, admin access, or recipient delivery proof. No timed freshness guarantee is required.

## Current behaviour and project evidence

- [PRODUCT.md](PRODUCT.md) defines CAP-03 as the latest authorised sender status lookup for a previously accepted parcel and SEC-01 as sender access to their own parcels only.
- [GLOSSARY.md](GLOSSARY.md) defines a receipt as a durable acknowledgement that the relay accepted a parcel.
- [src/status-contract.txt](src/status-contract.txt) records the existing `findReceipt(receiptId)` result as `{receiptId, senderId, currentStatus, updatedAt}` or not-found. Existing authentication exposes `senderId` from a validated session. A browser status page does not yet exist.

## Required behaviour

1. A sender opens a receipt status link. If their session has expired, the browser requires sign-in and preserves the requested destination so they can return to the same receipt status view after authentication.
2. During a lookup, the browser announces the loading state to screen-reader users.
3. The authenticated lookup uses the validated session's `senderId` and the existing `findReceipt(receiptId)` contract. It checks ownership before returning receipt details. For an owned receipt, the read-only response contains `receiptId`, `currentStatus`, and `updatedAt`; it does not expose `senderId`.
4. The page shows the latest successfully read status and its update time for an owned receipt. The allowed status values are **Accepted**, **In transit**, **Delivered**, and **Failed**.
5. A missing receipt and a receipt owned by another sender produce the same unavailable response and the same browser outcome. Neither response reveals whether the receipt exists or who owns it.
6. A request failure provides error feedback and a retry action. If the page has a previous successful read, it remains visible and is marked stale while the error is shown. Retry performs another read; displayed status changes only when that read succeeds. If there is no previous successful read, the error and retry action remain available without showing a status.
7. Keyboard and screen-reader users can reach and understand the complete outcome, including the status and update time, unavailable state, sign-in return, loading state, and error and retry state.

## Solution constraints

The status response is read-only and has no write path. The existing data source and validated session contract remain in use. This feature requires no migration or new dependency.

## Acceptance criteria

- Given a valid session and an owned receipt, opening its link displays its current allowed status and `updatedAt` from the latest successful read.
- Given an unknown receipt or one owned by a different sender, lookup returns the same unavailable response and the page presents the same unavailable message in both cases, with no receipt details disclosed.
- Given an expired session, opening a receipt status link requires sign-in and returns the sender to that receipt status destination after authentication.
- Given a pending read, loading is announced. Given a failed read, an accessible error and retry action are available.
- Given a successful read followed by a failed read, the last successful status and update time remain visible with stale feedback. A retry does not show a new status unless its read succeeds.
- The status view and all its outcomes can be used with a keyboard and understood with a screen reader.

## Verification seams

Verify the authenticated lookup's ownership check, allowed response fields, and identical missing and forbidden outcomes. Verify the browser interaction for owned and unavailable receipts, sign-in return, announced loading, accessible error and retry, and preservation of the last successful read after failure.

docs/features/sender-receipt-status/spec.content:
# Sender receipt-status view

> **Authority:** This document owns the confirmed intent and selected solution for this feature. It is ready for ticket decomposition.

## Feature overview

A sender who opens a receipt status link can see the latest status of their accepted parcel and when that status was updated. This refines [CAP-03 and SEC-01](../../../PRODUCT.md). A [receipt](../../../GLOSSARY.md) acknowledges parcel acceptance; the view does not provide proof of delivery to the recipient. The intent and solution below are confirmed in [the feature decision](../../../confirmed-feature.md).

## Problem, outcomes, and success measures

The [current contract](../../../src/status-contract.txt) can find receipt data, and authentication supplies a sender identity, but there is no browser status page. The outcome is an accessible, sender-only view of the latest authorised status and its update time. No numeric success measure or timed freshness guarantee was selected.

## Scope and non-goals

### In scope

- An authenticated sender opens a receipt status link and reads the receipt's current status and update time.
- Missing and other senders' receipts produce the same unavailable outcome.
- Session expiry, loading, request failure and retry have the behaviour specified below.

### Non-goals

- Editing status, exporting records, live tracking, admin access or recipient delivery proof.

## Actors, goals, and use cases

### ACT-01 — Sender

The sender wants to know the latest status of a parcel they previously handed to the relay.

### UC-01 — Read an owned receipt status

- **Actor:** Sender.
- **Trigger:** Open a receipt status link.
- **Preconditions:** The receipt was accepted and belongs to the sender; the sender has a valid session or can sign in.
- **Successful outcome:** The page displays the receipt's latest status and update time.
- **Alternatives and exceptions:** An expired session sends the sender to sign-in and returns them to the requested destination afterward. An unknown or unowned receipt gives the same unavailable message. A request failure gives an error and a retry action; any last successful status remains visible with stale feedback until another read succeeds.

## Feature intent

### Requirements and rules

- **REQ-01 — Authorised status:** An authenticated sender can see the latest status and update time only for a receipt they own. The allowed statuses are **Accepted**, **In transit**, **Delivered** and **Failed**.
- **REQ-02 — Hidden ownership:** An unknown receipt and a receipt owned by another sender produce the same unavailable message, without revealing whether the receipt exists.
- **REQ-03 — Session return:** When a session has expired, the sender must sign in and then return to the receipt status destination they opened.
- **REQ-04 — Loading and recovery:** The page announces loading. A request failure offers retry. If a successful read precedes the failure, its status remains visible with stale and error feedback; a retry changes the displayed status only after a new read succeeds.
- **REQ-05 — Accessible outcome:** Keyboard and screen-reader users can reach and understand the status, update time, unavailable state, sign-in return, loading state, and error and retry state.

### Experience and design requirements

The page presents the current status and its update time together. Loading and errors are conveyed to assistive technology; retry is keyboard operable. Stale feedback distinguishes a retained successful result from a newly confirmed result.

### Scenarios and acceptance

#### SC-01 — Owned receipt

- **Given:** A signed-in sender opens a link to their accepted receipt.
- **When:** The status read succeeds.
- **Then:** The page shows one of the four allowed statuses and its update time for that receipt.

**Covers:** REQ-01, REQ-05.

#### SC-02 — Receipt unavailable

- **Given:** A signed-in sender opens a link to an unknown receipt or another sender's receipt.
- **When:** The status read completes.
- **Then:** Both cases show the same unavailable message and expose no receipt details.

**Covers:** REQ-02.

#### SC-03 — Session expired

- **Given:** A sender opens a receipt status link with an expired session.
- **When:** They complete sign-in.
- **Then:** They return to that receipt status destination, where the authenticated read determines the outcome.

**Covers:** REQ-03.

#### SC-04 — Failed read and retry

- **Given:** The page has displayed a successful status read.
- **When:** A later read fails and the sender retries.
- **Then:** The page retains the last successful status, identifies it as stale, announces the error and offers retry; no new status is displayed unless a subsequent read succeeds.

**Covers:** REQ-04, REQ-05.

#### SC-05 — Initial loading and failure

- **Given:** A sender opens a receipt status link and no status has yet been read successfully.
- **When:** The read is pending and then fails.
- **Then:** Loading is announced while pending; the error is announced and retry is keyboard operable after failure. No status is presented as a successful read.

**Covers:** REQ-04, REQ-05.

#### Acceptance conditions

- **ACC-01:** The status lookup and browser interaction together demonstrate authorised read, indistinguishable unavailable outcomes, sign-in return, and accessible loading and recovery through their stable observable boundaries.

## Selected solution

### Design drivers and current context

[Product intent](../../../PRODUCT.md) limits status lookup to the sender's own parcel and excludes recipient proof. The [current contract](../../../src/status-contract.txt) has `findReceipt(receiptId)` returning `{receiptId, senderId, currentStatus, updatedAt}` or not-found; existing authentication exposes `senderId` from a validated session. The browser status page does not yet exist. The [confirmed decision](../../../confirmed-feature.md) selects reuse of both contracts and requires ownership filtering before details are returned.

### Strategy and material decisions

Provide a browser receipt status page backed by an authenticated, read-only lookup. Compare the receipt's `senderId` with the validated session's `senderId` before returning status details. Map not-found and ownership mismatch to one unavailable response. Keep the existing receipt data source and session contract; add no write path, migration or dependency. No timed freshness promise is part of this solution.

### Responsibilities and boundaries

The browser owns loading, display, sign-in return, stale feedback and retry interaction. The authenticated lookup owns sender scoping and the public status result. `findReceipt` supplies the current receipt record; its `senderId` is used inside the ownership boundary and is not exposed in the status response.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    B[Browser status page] -->|receiptId; validated session| L[Authenticated status lookup]
    L -->|findReceipt receiptId| R[Existing receipt source]
    L -->|owned status or unavailable| B
```

### Interfaces and data contracts

- The authenticated status read takes the receipt identifier from the opened destination and the sender identity from the validated session.
- An owned receipt returns a read-only response containing `receiptId`, `currentStatus` and `updatedAt`. `currentStatus` is one of **Accepted**, **In transit**, **Delivered** or **Failed**.
- Missing and forbidden receipts return the same unavailable response. Request failure is distinguishable so the browser can offer retry; it does not imply that the receipt is unavailable.
- The existing `findReceipt` shape and validated-session identity contract remain the source-side inputs. No transport route or presentation format is prescribed by this feature decision.

### Data and lifecycle

The feature reads the existing receipt data. `updatedAt` accompanies the latest returned status. There is no status edit or new persistent data, so no data migration is required. A successful response becomes the browser's last successful read; a failed later request does not replace it. A later successful read replaces it with the newly returned status and update time.

### Integrations and failure handling

Session validation precedes any status disclosure. On expiry, sign-in preserves the requested receipt destination and the page reads it after return. Lookup applies ownership before returning details; missing and forbidden records share one unavailable outcome. A failed read leaves any last successful result visible with stale and error feedback, and retry starts another read.

### Cross-cutting and operational design

The ownership check enforces [SEC-01](../../../PRODUCT.md) at the status response boundary. The browser experience must work with keyboard and screen reader, including announced loading and error states. Existing data source and session behaviour remain in use. There is no new dependency, migration or timed freshness guarantee.

### Verification seams

- Authenticated status lookup: owned response fields and allowed values; identical unavailable result for unknown and unowned receipts; no status disclosure before ownership validation.
- Browser interaction: status with update time, sign-in return destination, announced loading, and accessible error, stale and retry behaviour; a new status appears only after a successful read.

## Dependencies, assumptions, risks, and unresolved items

- **DEP-01 — Existing contracts:** `findReceipt` and validated-session `senderId` are [current-system inputs](../../../src/status-contract.txt) to the selected read path. REQ-01 and REQ-02 depend on them.
- **RSK-01 — Ownership disclosure:** Divergent handling of missing and unowned receipts could reveal existence. The shared unavailable response and ownership check before detail return address REQ-02.
- **Unresolved items:** None. The [confirmed feature decision](../../../confirmed-feature.md) states that all behavioural, contract and structural choices are accepted.

## Traceability and readiness

| Intent or acceptance | Selected responsibility or contract | Verification seam |
| --- | --- | --- |
| REQ-01, REQ-02 | Authenticated, sender-scoped read-only response | Status lookup outcomes |
| REQ-03 | Preserve destination through sign-in | Browser sign-in return |
| REQ-04, REQ-05 | Loading, retained result, stale and error feedback, retry | Browser interaction and assistive technology |
| ACC-01 | Lookup and page together | Both stable boundaries |

| Introduced design element | Origin |
| --- | --- |
| Status page and response fields | REQ-01; [confirmed solution](../../../confirmed-feature.md) |
| Ownership check and common unavailable response | REQ-02, SEC-01 |
| Existing receipt and session contracts | [Current contract](../../../src/status-contract.txt); confirmed solution |
| Sign-in return and retained result on failure | REQ-03, REQ-04 |

### Readiness statement

The confirmed intent, response boundary, ownership rule, recovery behaviour and verification seams are specified. Ticket decomposition can proceed without choosing product behaviour or a material solution.

import unittest
from shipping import shipping_cost
class ShippingTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_shipping_cost_tiers(self):
        cases = (
            (0, 3),
            (1000, 3),
            (1001, 7),
            (5000, 7),
            (5001, 12),
        )
        for weight_grams, expected in cases:
            with self.subTest(weight_grams=weight_grams):
                self.assertEqual(shipping_cost(weight_grams), expected)

- Suggested direction: Preserve provider idempotency across the failure and retry path.

docs/features/receipt-status-view/ticket.content:
# TKT-001: View an owned receipt status

- **Status:** Todo
- **Complexity:** 2
- **Blocked by:** None
- **Blocks:** [TKT-002](TKT-002-recover-receipt-status-reads.md)
- **Authority:** [Approved work](../../../../approved-work.md); [confirmed proposal, item 1](../../../../confirmed-proposal.md)

## Outcome

A session-authenticated sender can use the browser and status lookup to see the current status and update time of an owned receipt. An unknown receipt ID and an ID belonging to another sender produce the same unavailable response.

## Context

The existing session and receipt store supply `senderId`, `currentStatus`, and `updatedAt`. The initial statuses are Accepted, In transit, Delivered, and Failed. This is a read-only view: export, editing, admin controls, and live tracking are outside scope. No new dependency or migration is approved. Authenticated lookup and browser interactions are the stable verification boundaries.

## Functional requirements

- The status lookup returns a receipt's current status and update time only when its `senderId` matches the authenticated sender.
- Unknown and other-sender receipt IDs yield indistinguishable unavailable responses.
- The browser presents the owned receipt's status and update time, including each initial status, and presents loading and unavailable states.

## Non-functional requirements

- Loading and unavailable states are usable by keyboard and conveyed to screen readers.
- The view and lookup remain read-only and use the existing session and receipt store without a new dependency or migration.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An authenticated sender can look up and view an owned receipt's current status and `updatedAt` value in the browser for Accepted, In transit, Delivered, and Failed.
- [ ] The lookup gives the same unavailable response for an unknown ID and an ID owned by another sender; the browser does not reveal either receipt's details.
- [ ] Keyboard and screen-reader users can perceive the browser's loading and unavailable states.
- [ ] Reading status does not change receipt data or provide export, editing, admin, or live-tracking controls.

# TKT-002: Recover receipt status reads

- **Status:** Todo
- **Complexity:** 3
- **Blocked by:** [TKT-001](TKT-001-view-an-owned-receipt-status.md)
- **Blocks:** None
- **Authority:** [Approved work](../../../../approved-work.md); [confirmed proposal, item 2](../../../../confirmed-proposal.md)

## Outcome

When a receipt status read fails, the browser preserves the last successfully read status with accessible stale, error, and retry feedback. After a session expires, sign-in returns the sender to the intended receipt destination.

## Context

This extends the authenticated, read-only receipt lookup and browser status view in TKT-001. The existing session and receipt store remain the sources of identity and status; no new dependency or migration is approved. Export, editing, admin controls, and live tracking remain outside scope. Browser interactions are the stable verification boundary.

## Functional requirements

- A network failure during a status read leaves the last successfully read status visible and identifies it as stale while showing error and retry feedback.
- A retry replaces the visible status only after a successful read.
- When a session expires, sign-in preserves and restores the intended receipt destination.

## Non-functional requirements

- Stale, error, and retry states are usable by keyboard and conveyed to screen readers.
- Recovery stays read-only and uses the existing session and receipt store without a new dependency or migration.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After a successful status read, a network failure leaves that status and update time visible, marks the information as stale, and presents an error and retry action.
- [ ] A failed retry retains the last successful status and stale feedback; a successful retry updates the visible status and update time and clears stale feedback.
- [ ] After an expired session interrupts an intended receipt visit, completing sign-in returns the sender to that receipt destination, subject to the owned-receipt lookup boundary.
- [ ] Keyboard and screen-reader users can perceive stale and error feedback and operate retry.

# TKT-001 — View an owned receipt status

- **Status:** Todo
- **Complexity:** 2
- **Blocked by:** None
- **Blocks:** TKT-002
- **Authority:** [Approved work](../../../../approved-work.md); [confirmed proposal](../../../../confirmed-proposal.md), item 1.

## Outcome

An authenticated sender can use the browser and status lookup to see the current status and update time of an owned receipt. Unknown and other senders' receipt IDs yield the same unavailable response, and loading and unavailable states are accessible.

## Context

The existing session and receipt store supply `senderId`, `currentStatus`, and `updatedAt`. The initial status vocabulary is Accepted, In transit, Delivered, and Failed. This view is read-only. Export, editing, admin controls, and live tracking are outside the approved scope.

## Functional requirements

- Require a sender session for receipt status lookup and show only receipts owned by that sender.
- Return the same unavailable result for an unknown receipt ID and a receipt owned by another sender, without exposing either receipt's status or update time.
- Show an owned receipt's current status and update time in the browser, including each initial status.
- Provide loading and unavailable browser states.

## Non-functional requirements

- Keep the feature read-only and use the existing session and receipt store without new dependencies or migration.
- Make loading and unavailable states usable by keyboard and screen reader users.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With an authenticated sender and owned receipt, status lookup and browser display agree on `currentStatus` and `updatedAt` for Accepted, In transit, Delivered, and Failed.
- [ ] An unknown receipt ID and another sender's receipt ID produce indistinguishable unavailable lookup and browser results, with neither status nor update time disclosed.
- [ ] A sender without a valid session cannot retrieve receipt status through the lookup.
- [ ] Keyboard and screen reader users can perceive loading and unavailable browser states.

# TKT-002 — Recover receipt status reads

- **Status:** Todo
- **Complexity:** 3
- **Blocked by:** TKT-001
- **Blocks:** None
- **Authority:** [Approved work](../../../../approved-work.md); [confirmed proposal](../../../../confirmed-proposal.md), item 2.

## Outcome

After a failed receipt status read, the browser preserves the last successful status with accessible stale, error, and retry feedback. If the sender's session expires, sign-in restores the intended receipt destination.

## Context

This ticket builds on the accepted authenticated lookup and browser status view in TKT-001. The feature remains read-only, uses the existing session and receipt store, and has no export, editing, admin controls, or live tracking.

## Functional requirements

- When a network read fails after a successful read, keep the last successful status and update time visible and identify them as stale alongside error and retry feedback.
- Let the sender retry a failed read; replace the displayed status and update time only after a successful retry.
- When a session has expired, direct the sender through sign-in and restore the intended receipt destination afterward.

## Non-functional requirements

- Make stale, error, and retry states usable by keyboard and screen reader users.
- Use the existing session and receipt store without new dependencies or migration.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Following a successful status read, a network failure leaves the last successful status and update time visible with perceivable stale and error feedback.
- [ ] Keyboard and screen reader users can perceive the stale and error feedback and operate retry.
- [ ] An unsuccessful retry does not replace the last successful status or update time; a successful retry updates them to the newly read values.
- [ ] After session expiry, sign-in returns the sender to the receipt destination they intended to view, where authenticated status lookup resumes.

# Parcel Relay

> **Authority:** This document owns confirmed whole-product intent and system-wide requirements. Feature specifications refine it without silently changing it.

## Executive summary

Parcel Relay gives small independent couriers a trustworthy place to receive parcel dispatch requests and gives sender organisations durable evidence that a request was accepted. Senders use a browser to submit parcels, obtain receipts, check status, and export their data. Courier dispatchers work from accepted parcels and update their status; courier administrators control sender access. The product must prevent duplicate acceptance after a lost acknowledgement, keep accepted receipts through service restart, and isolate each sender's records. It does not manage routes, drivers, billing, or proof of delivery to a recipient.

## Purpose, problem, and vision

Dispatch requests can be lost or duplicated when senders and couriers lack a dependable record of acceptance. Parcel Relay establishes one durable acceptance record for each accepted parcel and makes its latest status visible to the sender. After an interruption, dispatchers can reconcile the accepted parcels they remain responsible for.

## Users, actors, stakeholders, and needs

- **Sender organisations:** Submit parcels, know whether a request was refused or accepted, retain a stable receipt, check status, and export their records without seeing another sender's parcels.
- **Courier dispatchers:** See accepted parcels, track their progress, update status, and reconcile their queue after service recovery.
- **Courier administrators:** Authorise and revoke sender access while preserving authorised access to prior records for the configured retention period.
- **Recipients:** Their addresses are processed for dispatch; they do not use the product or receive a product acknowledgement.

No third-party approval body participates in acceptance.

## Value, goals, and success measures

The product aims to avoid lost or duplicate dispatch requests. Its observable success measures are that a sender can submit one parcel, see one durable receipt, and obtain its latest status; a retry after acknowledgement loss does not create another accepted parcel; and dispatcher reconciliation accounts for accepted parcels after service recovery. No measured baseline, target volume, or numerical service threshold has been established.

## Scope, boundaries, and non-goals

### In scope

- Sender access administration and revocation.
- Parcel submission, explicit refusal of invalid requests, acceptance receipts, and safe retry after acknowledgement loss.
- Dispatcher queue, status updates, recovery reconciliation, and sender status lookup.
- Sender data export and lifecycle duties for retained acceptance evidence and recipient addresses.

### Non-goals

- Route optimisation and driver location tracking.
- Billing.
- Proof that a recipient received a parcel.

## Key journeys

### Sender access, submission, and acknowledgement

**Actors:** Courier administrator, sender organisation, Parcel Relay.

An administrator authorises a sender (CAP-01). The sender submits a parcel (CAP-02). An invalid request receives an explicit refusal without acceptance. A valid request becomes an accepted parcel with a durable receipt (CAP-03). If the acknowledgement is lost, the sender can retry and recover the same acceptance and receipt under QUAL-01 and INT-01.

### Dispatch, status, and recovery

**Actors:** Courier dispatcher, sender organisation, Parcel Relay.

A dispatcher sees accepted parcels in the queue (CAP-04), updates their status (CAP-05), and reconciles accepted parcels after service recovery under OPS-01. The sender checks the latest status, with its freshness visible under QUAL-02. The journey ends when the sender has the current recorded status; the product makes no claim that the recipient received the parcel.

### Export and access exit

**Actors:** Sender organisation, courier administrator, Parcel Relay.

The sender exports its records (CAP-06). An administrator may revoke sender access (CAP-01), stopping new submissions while authorised prior records remain accessible for the configured retention period under SEC-02. Data lifecycle duties are governed by DATA-02 and the unresolved retention duration in OQ-01.

## Functional capabilities

### Access and parcel acceptance

#### CAP-01: Sender access administration

- **Actors and value:** Courier administrators control which sender organisations may use the relay; senders can use authorised access.
- **High-level responsibility:** Authorise and revoke sender access to product functions and records.
- **Boundaries:** Revocation governs new submissions and access to prior records as specified by SEC-02; it does not itself delete acceptance evidence.
- **Source trace:** Confirmed foundation, scope and access journey.

#### CAP-02: Parcel submission and refusal

- **Actors and value:** Sender organisations can request dispatch and understand when a request has not been accepted.
- **High-level responsibility:** Receive parcel requests and explicitly refuse invalid submissions without accepting a parcel.
- **Boundaries:** Acceptance acknowledgement is CAP-03; detailed validation rules belong to a later feature specification.
- **Source trace:** Confirmed foundation, submission journey and external sender contract.

#### CAP-03: Acceptance receipt

- **Actors and value:** Sender organisations and dispatchers have durable evidence of an accepted parcel.
- **High-level responsibility:** Acknowledge accepted parcels with a stable receipt that the sender can obtain after submission or retry.
- **Boundaries:** Receipt means acceptance by the relay, not delivery to a recipient. Retry behaviour is governed by QUAL-01.
- **Source trace:** Confirmed foundation, purpose, submission journey and product-level acceptance.

### Dispatch and sender visibility

#### CAP-04: Dispatcher queue and reconciliation

- **Actors and value:** Dispatchers can find accepted parcels and account for them after interruption.
- **High-level responsibility:** Present accepted parcels for dispatch work and reconciliation.
- **Boundaries:** Does not optimise routes or track drivers; recovery is governed by OPS-01.
- **Source trace:** Confirmed foundation, dispatcher journey and recovery requirement.

#### CAP-05: Parcel status management and lookup

- **Actors and value:** Dispatchers record progress; senders can see the latest recorded status of their parcels.
- **High-level responsibility:** Allow dispatchers to update parcel status and authorised senders to look it up.
- **Boundaries:** Status is the relay's recorded dispatch status, not proof of receipt by a recipient; freshness is governed by QUAL-02.
- **Source trace:** Confirmed foundation, dispatcher and sender needs and status journey.

### Sender records

#### CAP-06: Sender data export

- **Actors and value:** Sender organisations can take a usable record of their accepted parcels.
- **High-level responsibility:** Export a sender's records with receipt identity and status history.
- **Boundaries:** Export remains subject to sender isolation and the data lifecycle obligations in DATA-01 and DATA-02; detailed export and deletion rules await OQ-01.
- **Source trace:** Confirmed foundation, scope, export journey and system-wide export requirement.

## Quality requirements

### QUAL-01: Single acceptance across retry

When a sender retries a submission after its acknowledgement is lost, the relay must preserve one accepted parcel and one stable receipt for that request. This is observable through the sender's recovered receipt and the dispatcher's accepted-parcel record.

- **Source:** Confirmed foundation, lost-acknowledgement journey and product-level acceptance.
- **Scope:** CAP-02, CAP-03, CAP-04 and the sender contract.

### QUAL-02: Visible status freshness

The sender's status view must make the freshness of the latest recorded status visible, so a sender can distinguish a current observation from an older one.

- **Source:** Confirmed foundation, system-wide status requirement.
- **Scope:** CAP-05 and sender status lookup.

### QUAL-03: Accessible browser use

Sender, dispatcher, and administrator functions must be usable through a web browser with keyboard and assistive-technology support.

- **Source:** Confirmed foundation, system-wide access requirement.
- **Scope:** All browser-facing capabilities and journeys.

## System context and external interfaces

Sender organisations, courier dispatchers, and courier administrators interact with Parcel Relay through browsers. The relay owns its acceptance receipts, parcel status records, and sender access decisions. Recipient addresses cross from senders into the relay for dispatch. No third-party approval service is part of the acceptance boundary.

### INT-01: Sender-facing acceptance contract

The external sender contract must expose stable receipt identifiers for accepted parcels and explicit errors for invalid requests. A refused request must not be represented as accepted. The same accepted request must retain its receipt identity after an acknowledgement is lost and the sender retries.

- **Source:** Confirmed foundation, external sender contract and submission journey.
- **Scope:** CAP-02, CAP-03 and sender-facing interactions.

## Data and information requirements

### DATA-01: Receipt and status record integrity

The relay must preserve the identity of each accepted parcel's receipt and its status history in sender exports. The exported identity must correspond to the sender-visible receipt and the dispatcher's accepted-parcel record.

- **Source:** Confirmed foundation, export requirement and product-level acceptance.
- **Scope:** CAP-03, CAP-04, CAP-05 and CAP-06.

### DATA-02: Recipient-address purpose and lifecycle

The relay must handle recipient addresses only for dispatch. Export and deletion duties must respect retained acceptance evidence; the exact retention duration remains unresolved in OQ-01 and must be set before export/deletion is specified.

- **Source:** Confirmed foundation, recipient-address and data lifecycle requirements, and explicit open item.
- **Scope:** Recipient addresses, acceptance evidence, CAP-02, CAP-04 and CAP-06.

## Integrations and external dependencies

No external system or third-party approval body is required by the confirmed foundation. The sender-facing contract is INT-01. No endpoint, protocol, adapter, or vendor has been selected.

## Security, privacy, safety, and compliance

### SEC-01: Sender record isolation

The relay must prevent one sender organisation from accessing another sender's parcels, receipts, statuses, or exports. Cross-sender access is a failure of the product-level acceptance condition.

- **Source:** Confirmed foundation, access-control requirement and product-level acceptance.
- **Scope:** CAP-02, CAP-03, CAP-05, CAP-06 and sender-facing records.

### SEC-02: Revocation and prior records

Administrators must be able to revoke sender access so that new submissions stop, while authorised prior records remain accessible for the configured retention period. This requirement does not establish the duration, which is OQ-01.

- **Source:** Confirmed foundation, revocation journey and non-blocking retention item.
- **Scope:** CAP-01, CAP-02, CAP-05, CAP-06 and retained sender records.

## Technology and platform constraints

### TECH-01: Existing EU hosting region

Parcel Relay must be hosted in the existing EU region. This is a hard hosting constraint; the foundation does not mandate a database, driver, runtime, or internal component design.

- **Source:** Confirmed foundation, system-wide hosting requirement.
- **Scope:** Hosted product and its retained data.

## Operational and lifecycle requirements

### OPS-01: Acceptance durability and recovery

Accepted receipts must survive service restart, and dispatchers must be able to reconcile all accepted parcels after service recovery. Reconciliation must account for acceptance even when the sender's acknowledgement was lost.

- **Source:** Confirmed foundation, recovery journey and system-wide durability requirement.
- **Scope:** CAP-03, CAP-04 and accepted-parcel records.

## Assumptions, dependencies, constraints, risks, and open questions

- **Constraint `CON-01`: Existing EU region:** The confirmed hosting constraint is TECH-01. A change to the hosting region requires a new product decision.
- **Open question `OQ-01`: What is the exact retention duration?** The confirmed foundation leaves this non-blocking for whole-product definition. Choosing it incorrectly could keep recipient address data too long or remove reconciliation evidence too soon, affecting DATA-02, SEC-02 and CAP-06. Resolve the duration with the user before specifying export/deletion; no deletion duration is promised here.

## Product-level acceptance and foundation readiness

### Product-level acceptance

- **ACC-01:** Across a sender's submit, retry, and status journey and a dispatcher's recovery journey, the relay preserves one accepted parcel and one stable receipt for the request, lets the sender obtain its latest recorded status, accounts for the accepted parcel after recovery, and prevents cross-sender access.

### Foundation readiness

The confirmed direction covers sender entry and refusal, acceptance and retry, dispatcher work and recovery, sender status and export, and access exit. The capabilities and system requirements above provide a boundary for later feature specification. OQ-01 is the sole confirmed non-blocking item and must be resolved before export/deletion is specified. There is no shipped system to inspect, so the document states target requirements rather than observed behaviour.

## Evidence and traceability

- [Confirmed foundation](confirmed-foundation.md): User-confirmed whole-product direction, requirements, product-level acceptance, and exact document effect.
- [Glossary](GLOSSARY.md): Shared meanings of **Parcel** and **Receipt**.
- [Project guidance](AGENTS.md): Directs use of the root glossary.

No shipped system, applicable ADR, or research report was supplied.

# Parcel Relay — Product Requirements

## Purpose and users

Parcel Relay gives small independent couriers a trustworthy place to receive dispatch requests and gives sender organisations durable acknowledgement of acceptance. Courier dispatchers accept and track requests. Senders submit parcels, retain a record of acceptance, and view the latest status. Courier administrators manage sender access. The product does not require approval by a third party.

## Goal and success

The product aims to prevent lost or duplicate requests. A successful sender journey submits one parcel, receives one durable receipt, and can obtain the parcel's latest status. After service recovery, dispatcher reconciliation accounts for accepted parcels. No measured baseline or target volume has been established.

## Product boundaries

The product includes sender access, parcel submission, acceptance receipts, a dispatcher queue and status updates, sender status lookup, administrative revocation of sender access, and sender data export.

Route optimisation, driver location tracking, billing, and proof that a recipient received a parcel are outside the product scope.

## End-to-end journeys

1. A courier administrator authorises a sender to use the service.
2. The sender submits a parcel. An invalid submission receives an explicit explanation of refusal and is not accepted. A valid submission is accepted and yields a durable receipt.
3. A dispatcher sees the accepted parcel in the queue and updates its delivery status. The sender can view the latest status or export its data.
4. If the receipt acknowledgement is lost, the sender can retry without creating another accepted parcel or a new receipt identity.
5. After service recovery, dispatchers can reconcile all accepted parcels.
6. When sender access is revoked, new submissions stop. Previously authorised records remain accessible for the configured retention period, subject to access control.

## Product and system requirements

### Access and usability

- The service must be accessible through a web browser and support keyboard use and assistive technology.
- Access control must isolate each sender's parcels from other senders.
- Courier administrators must be able to authorise and revoke sender access. Revocation must prevent new submissions while preserving access to previously authorised records for the configured retention period.

### Acceptance and recovery

- Each accepted parcel must have one stable, durable receipt identity.
- A lost acknowledgement followed by a retry must not result in duplicate acceptance.
- Accepted receipts must survive a service restart.
- Dispatchers must be able to see accepted parcels and reconcile them after service recovery.
- The external sender contract must provide stable receipt identifiers and explicit errors for invalid requests.

### Status and export

- Dispatchers must be able to update delivery status, and senders must be able to obtain the latest status of their parcels.
- The freshness of status information must be visible to senders.
- Sender data exports must preserve receipt identity and status history.

### Data handling and hosting

- Recipient addresses must be handled only for the dispatch purpose.
- Export and deletion duties must respect retained evidence of acceptance.
- The service must be hosted in the existing EU region.

## Product-level acceptance

The sender's submission, retry, and status journey and the dispatcher's recovery journey must preserve one accepted parcel and one stable receipt, while preventing access across senders.

## Open question

**OQ — Retention duration:** The exact retention duration must be agreed with the user before detailed export and deletion requirements are specified. Choosing incorrectly could keep recipient address data too long or remove reconciliation evidence too soon. This decision affects export, deletion, and data lifecycle requirements. No deletion duration is promised here. The question does not block the product boundaries or the other capabilities above.

## Evidence and status

This document reflects the user-confirmed direction in `confirmed-foundation.md`. No shipped system exists yet.

# Parcel Relay

> **Authority:** This document owns confirmed whole-product intent and system-wide requirements. Feature specifications refine it without silently changing it.

## Executive summary

Parcel Relay gives small independent couriers a trustworthy place to receive dispatch requests and gives sender organisations a durable record that a request was accepted. Courier dispatchers work from accepted parcels and update their status; senders can check status and export their records. The product must avoid lost or duplicate requests, protect each sender's information, and run in the existing EU hosting region. It does not cover route optimisation, driver tracking, billing, or proof of delivery to a recipient.

## Purpose, problem, and vision

Dispatch requests can be lost or accepted more than once when acknowledgement or service continuity fails. Parcel Relay exists so a sender can submit a parcel, know whether it was accepted, and follow its status, while a dispatcher can account for every accepted parcel after recovery. A **parcel** is a sender's delivery request; a **receipt** is the durable acknowledgement of its acceptance, as defined in [GLOSSARY.md](GLOSSARY.md).

## Users, actors, stakeholders, and needs

- **Sender organisation:** Submits parcels and needs a dependable acceptance record, current status view, and export of its data.
- **Courier dispatcher:** Needs a queue of accepted parcels, the ability to update status, and a way to reconcile accepted work after service recovery.
- **Courier administrator:** Authorises and revokes sender access while preserving appropriate access to prior records.
- **Recipient:** Their address is used for dispatch; they are a data subject, not a direct product user in the confirmed scope.

No third-party approval body is required.

## Value, goals, and success measures

The product's value is fewer lost or duplicate dispatch requests and a shared, durable account of acceptance. Success is observable when a sender submits one parcel, sees one stable receipt, and obtains its latest status, and when dispatcher reconciliation accounts for accepted parcels after service recovery. Product-level acceptance is defined in [ACC-01](#product-level-acceptance). No measured baseline, target volume, or numerical service threshold has been confirmed.

## Scope, boundaries, and non-goals

### In scope

- Sender access and administrative revocation.
- Parcel submission, explicit refusal of invalid requests, and durable acceptance receipts.
- Dispatcher queue, status updates, and reconciliation after recovery.
- Sender status lookup and data export.
- Appropriate retention and deletion of recipient address data and acceptance evidence.

### Non-goals

- Route optimisation or driver location tracking.
- Billing.
- Proof that a recipient received a parcel.

## Key journeys

### Access, submission, and acceptance

**Actors:** Courier administrator, sender organisation, courier dispatcher.

An administrator authorises a sender through [CAP-01](#cap-01--sender-access). The sender submits a parcel through [CAP-02](#cap-02--parcel-submission). An invalid request receives an explicit refusal without acceptance. A valid request produces the durable [CAP-03](#cap-03--acceptance-receipt) receipt and enters the dispatcher's [CAP-04](#cap-04--dispatcher-queue) queue. If acknowledgement is lost, a sender retry preserves the original acceptance and receipt.

### Dispatch and status

**Actors:** Courier dispatcher, sender organisation.

The dispatcher tracks accepted work in the queue and updates parcel status through [CAP-05](#cap-05--status-updates). The sender uses [CAP-06](#cap-06--sender-status-lookup) to see the latest status and its freshness. After service recovery, dispatchers reconcile accepted parcels against durable acceptance evidence.

### Records, revocation, and exit

**Actors:** Courier administrator, sender organisation.

The sender exports its records through [CAP-07](#cap-07--sender-data-export). An administrator can revoke the sender's ability to make new submissions through [CAP-01](#cap-01--sender-access). Prior records remain accessible to authorised users for the configured retention period, then follow the data lifecycle requirements. The exact period remains [OQ-01](#oq-01--exact-retention-duration).

## Functional capabilities

### Sender access and requests

#### CAP-01 — Sender access

- **Actors and value:** Courier administrators control which sender organisations may submit requests; authorised users retain appropriate access to prior records.
- **High-level responsibility:** Authorise sender access and revoke the ability to make new submissions while maintaining access to prior records for the configured retention period.
- **Boundaries:** Covers sender authorisation and revocation; parcel acceptance belongs to CAP-02 and CAP-03. It does not introduce third-party approval.
- **Source trace:** [Confirmed foundation](confirmed-foundation.md), administrator and revocation journeys.

#### CAP-02 — Parcel submission

- **Actors and value:** Sender organisations submit delivery requests and learn clearly whether a request was refused or accepted.
- **High-level responsibility:** Receive a parcel request and give an explicit invalid-request error without accepting an invalid parcel.
- **Boundaries:** Covers submission and refusal; durable acknowledgement and retry identity belong to CAP-03.
- **Source trace:** [Confirmed foundation](confirmed-foundation.md), submission journey and external sender contract.

#### CAP-03 — Acceptance receipt

- **Actors and value:** Senders obtain dependable evidence of acceptance; dispatchers can account for accepted work.
- **High-level responsibility:** Give each accepted parcel a durable receipt with a stable identifier and preserve that same acceptance when its acknowledgement is lost and the sender retries.
- **Boundaries:** Covers acceptance evidence and retry outcome; it does not prove delivery to a recipient.
- **Source trace:** [Confirmed foundation](confirmed-foundation.md), success goal and acknowledgement-loss journey.

### Dispatch and visibility

#### CAP-04 — Dispatcher queue

- **Actors and value:** Courier dispatchers see accepted parcels and can account for their work after service recovery.
- **High-level responsibility:** Present accepted parcels for dispatch tracking and reconciliation.
- **Boundaries:** Includes accepted work after recovery; route optimisation and driver location tracking are excluded.
- **Source trace:** [Confirmed foundation](confirmed-foundation.md), dispatcher need and recovery journey.

#### CAP-05 — Status updates

- **Actors and value:** Courier dispatchers record progress so senders can follow an accepted parcel.
- **High-level responsibility:** Allow dispatchers to update parcel status and retain its history for sender records.
- **Boundaries:** Covers status of accepted parcels; it does not assert recipient delivery proof.
- **Source trace:** [Confirmed foundation](confirmed-foundation.md), dispatcher and sender needs and export scope.

#### CAP-06 — Sender status lookup

- **Actors and value:** Sender organisations see the latest status of their own accepted parcels.
- **High-level responsibility:** Provide status lookup with visible freshness for authorised sender records.
- **Boundaries:** Covers sender visibility; dispatchers own status updates through CAP-05.
- **Source trace:** [Confirmed foundation](confirmed-foundation.md), sender need and status journey.

### Sender records

#### CAP-07 — Sender data export

- **Actors and value:** Sender organisations obtain their parcel records for their own use.
- **High-level responsibility:** Export authorised sender data with receipt identity and status history intact.
- **Boundaries:** Export and deletion follow the retained acceptance evidence obligation; the exact retention period is open in OQ-01.
- **Source trace:** [Confirmed foundation](confirmed-foundation.md), export scope and records journey.

## Quality requirements

### QUAL-01 — Accessible browser use

The sender, dispatcher, and administrator interactions must be usable through a web browser with keyboard and assistive-technology support; the applicable feature specifications must define verifiable interaction checks.

- **Source:** [Confirmed foundation](confirmed-foundation.md), system-wide access requirement.
- **Scope:** All user-facing journeys and capabilities.

### QUAL-02 — Visible status freshness

The sender status view must make the freshness of the displayed status visible, so a sender can judge whether the view reflects a recent update.

- **Source:** [Confirmed foundation](confirmed-foundation.md), sender status need and system-wide freshness requirement.
- **Scope:** CAP-06 and status information supplied by CAP-05.

## System context and external interfaces

Sender organisations, courier dispatchers, and courier administrators interact with the service through a browser. Senders provide parcel requests and receive refusal or receipt outcomes, status views, and exports. Dispatchers provide status updates; administrators control sender access. No external approval service or other integration is established by the confirmed foundation.

### INT-01 — Sender-facing acceptance contract

The sender-facing contract must expose stable receipt identifiers for accepted parcels and explicit errors for invalid requests. A retry after lost acknowledgement must resolve to the same accepted parcel and receipt, with no duplicate acceptance.

- **Source:** [Confirmed foundation](confirmed-foundation.md), external sender contract and acknowledgement-loss journey.
- **Scope:** CAP-02, CAP-03, and sender submission interactions. This is a hard external contract; its transport and payload are not selected here.

## Data and information requirements

### DATA-01 — Durable acceptance evidence

An accepted parcel and its receipt must survive service restart and remain available for dispatcher reconciliation.

- **Source:** [Confirmed foundation](confirmed-foundation.md), durable receipt and recovery requirements.
- **Scope:** CAP-03, CAP-04, and accepted parcel records.

### DATA-02 — Export integrity

Sender data exports must preserve each accepted parcel's receipt identity and status history.

- **Source:** [Confirmed foundation](confirmed-foundation.md), export requirement and sender record need.
- **Scope:** CAP-07 and records produced by CAP-03 and CAP-05.

### DATA-03 — Recipient address lifecycle

Recipient addresses must be handled only for the dispatch purpose. Export and deletion duties must respect retained acceptance evidence, and prior records must remain available to authorised users for the configured retention period. The duration is unresolved in OQ-01.

- **Source:** [Confirmed foundation](confirmed-foundation.md), purpose limitation, revocation, and retention direction.
- **Scope:** Recipient address data, CAP-01, CAP-07, and the lifecycle of accepted records.

## Integrations and external dependencies

No external integration is specified by the confirmed foundation, and no third-party approval body is required. The sender-facing contract is defined by [INT-01](#int-01--sender-facing-acceptance-contract); no transport or external system is mandated.

## Security, privacy, safety, and compliance

### SEC-01 — Sender isolation

Access control must prevent one sender organisation from accessing another sender's parcels, status, or exported records.

- **Source:** [Confirmed foundation](confirmed-foundation.md), system-wide sender isolation requirement.
- **Scope:** CAP-02, CAP-03, CAP-06, CAP-07, and all sender record access.

### SEC-02 — Revocation boundary

When a courier administrator revokes a sender's submission access, the service must reject new submissions from that sender while allowing authorised access to prior records during their configured retention period.

- **Source:** [Confirmed foundation](confirmed-foundation.md), administrative revocation and records journey.
- **Scope:** CAP-01, CAP-02, and access to existing records.

## Technology and platform constraints

### TECH-01 — Existing EU hosting region

The service must use the existing EU hosting region. This is a hard hosting constraint; no platform, database, runtime, or deployment topology is selected here.

- **Source:** [Confirmed foundation](confirmed-foundation.md), mandated hosting region.
- **Scope:** The service and its stored parcel, receipt, status, and recipient address data.

## Operational and lifecycle requirements

### OPS-01 — Recovery reconciliation

After service recovery, dispatchers must be able to reconcile all accepted parcels against durable acceptance evidence, including parcels whose sender acknowledgement was lost.

- **Source:** [Confirmed foundation](confirmed-foundation.md), dispatcher recovery and no-lost-request goal.
- **Scope:** CAP-03, CAP-04, and service recovery.

## Assumptions, dependencies, constraints, risks, and open questions

- **Assumptions:** None beyond the confirmed direction are needed for this foundation.
- **Dependencies:** No material external dependency is identified in the supplied evidence.
- **Constraints:** The hard sender-facing and hosting constraints are [INT-01](#int-01--sender-facing-acceptance-contract) and [TECH-01](#tech-01--existing-eu-hosting-region).
- **Risks:** The unresolved retention risk is recorded under OQ-01.

### OQ-01 — Exact retention duration

The [confirmed foundation](confirmed-foundation.md) leaves the period undecided. Choosing too long could retain recipient addresses unnecessarily; choosing too short could remove reconciliation evidence prematurely. It affects DATA-03, CAP-07, and the export and deletion lifecycle. The user owns the decision, to be resolved before the export/deletion feature specification. This does not block the product boundary or other feature specifications. No deletion duration is promised here.

## Product-level acceptance and foundation readiness

### Product-level acceptance

- **ACC-01:** Across a sender's submission, retry, and status journey and dispatcher recovery, one accepted parcel retains one stable receipt and remains accounted for, while cross-sender access is prevented. This is the whole-product outcome confirmed in the [foundation](confirmed-foundation.md).

### Foundation readiness

The confirmed handoff covers the intended actors, full submission and recovery path, sender records, administrative revocation, and system-wide constraints. It is sufficient to guide feature specifications except that export and deletion must wait for OQ-01. There is no shipped system evidence, measured baseline, target volume, or confirmed retention duration to assert.

## Evidence and traceability

- [Confirmed foundation](confirmed-foundation.md): User-confirmed intended direction, requirements, non-blocking open item, and exact document write.
- [GLOSSARY.md](GLOSSARY.md): Project meanings of parcel and receipt.
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): Repository guidance.

No shipped system, ADR, or research evidence was supplied or found in the repository.

docs/adr/0001-sender-generated-receipt-i.content:
# ADR 0001: Sender-generated receipt identifiers

Date: 2026-10-01

Status: Accepted

## Context

A receipt acknowledges that the relay accepted one parcel; it is distinct from a delivery confirmation. Receipts must remain identifiable when a relay instance is replaced. Existing clients retain sender identifiers for reconciliation, so changing identifier ownership later would be costly.

The relay generally uses instance-local identifiers. Receipts need an exception because their identity must persist across relay instances.

## Decision

The sender generates receipt identifiers. A receipt identifier is retained globally across relay instances instead of being generated independently by each relay.

## Rationale

Keeping the sender's identifier across relay replacements lets clients reconcile accepted parcels with the identifiers they already retain. It also keeps a retry after replacement tied to the same accepted parcel.

## Rejected alternative

Relay-local receipt identifiers with a translation table were considered. A retry after relay replacement could duplicate a parcel that had already been accepted, so this approach was rejected.

## Scope

This decision does not determine whether receipt export includes delivery confirmations. That external interface remains a separate decision.

## Decision

Senders generate receipt identifiers, which remain globally valid across relay instances. A receipt survives replacement of the relay that accepted its parcel. This is a deliberate exception to the relay's usual instance-local identifier policy.

# Keep receipts in an append-only journal

## Decision

Store receipts in an append-only journal and derive lookup projections from it. This preserves acceptance chronology when a receipt is replaced or corrected.

## Context

Consumers must be able to reconstruct the order of receipt acceptances after replacement. Overwriting receipt rows would erase that history, although mutable rows would be simpler to query. The existing delivery-status store uses mutable rows, but receipts require a different model. The receipt deduplication decision does not select a storage model.

## Consequences

Receipt lookups require maintained projections alongside the journal. Corrections add journal entries instead of replacing earlier acceptances, so consumers can recover the chronology. Export clients will use journal sequence positions; changing the storage model after deployment would therefore require changing that client-facing contract.

# Store receipts in an append-only journal

## Status
Accepted

## Context
The existing delivery-status store uses mutable rows. Receipt consumers need to reconstruct the chronology of acceptances after a receipt is replaced. Overwriting a receipt row would erase the correction history needed for that reconstruction.

The mutable-row alternative would be simpler to query, but it would not retain that history. The receipt retry deduplication decision in [ADR 0002](0002-receipt-deduplication.md) does not select a storage model.

## Decision
Store receipts in an append-only journal and build lookup projections from the journal. Do not overwrite receipt records when they are replaced. This intentionally differs from the mutable delivery-status store.

## Consequences
Consumers can reconstruct acceptance chronology, including replacements, from the journal. Lookup projections provide queryable views of the journal.

Existing export clients will use journal sequence positions. Changing the storage model after deployment would therefore be costly.
